Huge improvement: score 182,912 vs 3,585. Viewers 944. Great. Now we have 11 runs left (5-15). Need maximize final. We should use runs to identify further bottlenecks and improve. Score 182k likely decent but maybe can reach 300k+ or more. Need analyze run 4 logs/metrics to find bottlenecks. We have run 4 DB/NGINX app logs (access log disabled for API, but app no logger). We can inspect system metrics, MySQL status, maybe run custom load testing? We can use our own load generator? We shouldn't look up benchmarker source, but can generate traffic with scripts to test endpoints, not use benchmark. Could run `wrk`/`hey` if installed via proxy? But benchmark mix complex. We can analyze MySQL slow query log / performance_schema, but performance_schema disabled on s2. We can enable slow query log and general log? Enabling general log during benchmark slows; but one run for diagnosis is possible. Better use `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS` counters before/after run to see DB QPS, and `docker`? We can instrument app with a lightweight Prometheus? Or just inspect system CPU during a run. We can run run 5 with `vmstat`, `pidstat`, `mysqladmin ext` sampling to find bottlenecks. Each run costs one of 11. We can use run 5 as diagnostic with current config; but score will count. Final score is run 15; we can afford some diagnostic runs. We need plan.

Current architecture: s1 app+nginx+pdns+local MySQL(isudns), s2 MySQL. CPU on s1 maybe bottleneck (2 vCPU). s2 maybe high CPU due DB. Network between s1-s2. DNS water torture load increasing to 13 parallel; DNS on s1 with MySQL local. App on s1 uses CPU for JSON, caching. We can distribute app to s3 as second app to use more CPU, and perhaps split DB? s2 DB can handle. Need measure CPU during run.

We can use run 5 to monitor with a background script sampling `top`/`mpstat`/`mysqladmin` on s1 and s2 and nginx? But the benchmark is 60s; we can start monitoring before bench, collect. This doesn't alter load. Then analyze. Score on run 5 may be similar; final later better. We should first maybe inspect run 4's MySQL global status and performance (some counters reset? not). We can query `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS` now but includes run 2/3/4 etc and manual, but can compare with later. We can also use `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` for deadlocks etc. Let's gather current stats, CPU, app memory. Also check if app cache grew huge (user/livestream caches for benchmark-created ~? 1000 streams, 1000 users). Memory maybe okay.

Potential obvious improvements:
1. Use s3 as second app server to distribute TLS/JSON/Go CPU. Since DNS records for existing users all point to s1 after init. Need modify DNS zone load to alternate records between s1 and s3. But app's `POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS` on each app must be its own address for new users. Could run app on s3 pointing to s1 isudns remote for registration. Or simpler: keep app only on s1 for now; use s3 as read-only MySQL? Another approach: run second Go app on s3 with same DB s2, and configure DNS records to distribute half. Need update zone file `pdns/u.isucon.dev.zone` on s1 to use two addresses? init_zone.sh replaces `<ISUCON_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS>` with one address. We can modify `init_zone.sh` to alternate based on name hash or line number after substitution. But init.sh is executed by app on s1; we can edit `/home/isucon/webapp/pdns/init_zone.sh` to use two IPs. However the prompt says application must behave as docs; distributing subdomains is allowed. Need ensure all records, including pipe.u.isucon.dev and ns1, point to s1 because benchmark uses pipe for top/register/login and DNS server on s1. Only streamer subdomains can point s3. If we alternate all records including pipe, benchmark uses https://pipe.u.isucon.dev -> if points s3, s3 nginx must serve; could work, but initialize must go to s1 app so it can reset DB; if pipe points s3 app, s3 app's initialize runs its local init.sh (which may not be updated) and its env DB s2; could work if we deploy same code/files there. But safer keep pipe on s1 and alternate only user subdomains except pipe/ns1/mail etc. The zone file has 1000 seeded users + technical subdomains. We can modify `init_zone.sh` after `sed` substitution to run a Python/awk that changes A records for names not in a whitelist to alternate s1/s3 based on deterministic hash. But user registration direct insert in app uses `powerDNSSubdomainAddress` (s1) for new users on s1; new users created by benchmark will all hit s1, but only ~200 registrations vs 1000 seeded users and main viewer/streamer traffic. The benchmark may use newly registered users for some load; still s1. Could set app on s1 env to s1 and app on s3 env to s3; new users via pipe s1 will point s1. That's fine. Seeded users distribute 50/50. Could also configure s1 app to alternate new records between s1 and s3 for subsequent run? But direct insert function could choose based on username hash. Then new users distribute too. But app on s3 needs `POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS` for users created through s3 (if any requests route there). We can give s3 and s1 same algorithm selecting address by hash, independent of env, using two constants. But then `POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS` env unused/ignored; still spec? It should use allowed addresses. Could implement in addDNSRecord: choose `powerDNSSubdomainAddress` for all new users, or alternate. For now we can distribute seeded records and maybe new users via deterministic hash to s3 with code reading a second env address. More complexity.

But is app CPU actually bottleneck? Let's measure first. Use run 5 with monitoring. We'll start a monitoring script via ssh in background before bench, sampling every second for 70s:
- On s1: `vmstat 1 75` or `mpstat -P ALL 1 75` (sysstat maybe installed), `pidstat -p $(pgrep isupipe) 1`, nginx, mysqld local, pdns.
- On s2: `mpstat`, `pidstat mysqld`, `iostat`.
- MySQL global status snapshots before/after: `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS` maybe use `mysqladmin ext -i5`. Could gather QPS, threads_running, handler_reads, innodb row locks, slow queries.
- Also `ss -s` for connections.
- We can maybe instrument app with pprof? Could enable net/http/pprof on another port and sample CPU during run; but adding code and deploying could be done. Yet run 5 diagnostic should reflect current app. We can use Linux `perf`? Maybe not installed. `pidstat` from sysstat if installed. `top -b -n 1` every second. Use `vmstat`.

Let's check tools availability on servers (mpstat, pidstat, iostat, sar). Also check CPU steal. Then run monitoring during run 5. We can start background commands over ssh with nohup and collect files. Since benchmark run starts after a trigger; we can start monitors just before calling bench. They run 75s. The bench initialization takes ~8s + 60s load = ~70s; start monitor right before bench at 1s intervals for 90s. Good.

We have 11 runs, so one diagnostic is okay. But maybe we can infer from run 4 score and response times via benchmark logs? The wrapper only prints warnings and summary. It prints context canceled at end, not latency stats. Could inspect nginx access logs disabled; we can temporarily enable access log with `$request_time` for run 5 to analyze endpoint latency, but that adds overhead and writes lots; maybe manageable (~100k requests?). Run 4 total requests could be huge. We can log only API with `access_log /var/log/nginx/api.log combined;` and include `$request_time $upstream_response_time`. But logging every request may reduce score slightly, but diagnostic run. We can use a separate run 5 for profiling with access logs and maybe pprof. Or avoid altering and just CPU.

Actually we can get some app metrics by adding counters per endpoint in Go with atomic, and expose /debug/metrics; not needed. Nginx access log with upstream time is easiest and can handle. But logging ~ maybe 100k lines ~20MB; okay. We can enable access log for run 5 only, then disable. That gives endpoint counts and latency distribution, helping find hotspots. We also need know if requests are hitting timeouts or slow stats. Let's enable a custom log format `$time_iso8601 $host $request $status $request_time $upstream_response_time $body_bytes_sent` for API only. Use `access_log /var/log/nginx/api.log ...;` in location /api. Nginx reload. Start monitoring. Then run 5. Then analyze and disable log.

But run 5 may score slightly lower due logging; that's fine. We can then make improvements using run 6, etc. Final run 15.

Before run 5, maybe gather baseline MySQL status now. We can reset counters with `FLUSH STATUS` on s2 before run 5 to measure per-run. `FLUSH STATUS` resets global status (some). We can do that right before benchmark. Also on s1 local MySQL for DNS maybe. We'll gather `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS` after. We can use `mysqladmin -h 10.0.1.56 -uisucon -pisucon extended-status` before/after. Need not use app DB while benchmark runs except monitoring could add load; sample every 5s is negligible.

Let's check tools.

PDNS now active after auto-restart. The error `Host '127.0.0.1' is not allowed` arose because `skip-name-resolve` + existing user `'isudns'@'localhost'`? When connecting via TCP 127.0.0.1 with skip-name-resolve, host is 127.0.0.1, and user `'isudns'@'localhost'` doesn't match; `'isudns'@'%'` should match 127.0.0.1 though. Why not? Maybe `CREATE USER` was executed after pdns restart, so at 12:14:26 the `%` user wasn't created yet? In the command order: restart mysql, restart pdns, then create user. Yes, we created `'isudns'@'%'` after restart. PDNS auto-retry succeeded after user creation. Good. After reboot, `'isudns'@'%'` exists, so PDNS will connect. But to be safe, set PowerDNS gmysql host to 10.0.1.89 (matches `%`) or create `'isudns'@'127.0.0.1'`. We should create host-specific user and maybe keep localhost. Add `'isudns'@'127.0.0.1'` and `'isucon'@'127.0.0.1'`? PDNS uses isudns. Let's create to ensure. Also app dnsConn uses 127.0.0.1 with isudns; with skip-name-resolve it matches `%` now; fine. But add explicit anyway. We'll do later.

Now deploy s3 app. Need copy code to s3 `/home/isucon/webapp/go`, binary. On s3 current original app running. We'll stop, backup, deploy. Update env.sh. Modify service unit remove Requires/After mysql. Stop/disable pdns and mysql on s3 (but be careful app service requires mysql; after unit edit). Nginx config copy from s1. Use `/tmp/isupipe.conf` already on s1, but copy from workspace maybe. We'll scp. Ensure s3 `public` files and img. They exist. Set env:
```
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_ADDRESS="10.0.1.56"
...
ISUCON13_POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS="10.0.1.76"
ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS="10.0.1.89"
```
Keep DNS DB user/pass defaults. Maybe `ISUCON13_POWERDNS_DISABLED=false`.
Backup s3 env. Deploy code tar. Build binary local (already). scp to /tmp, stop app, install, start.

Need edit s3 service unit: use `sudo sed -i '/^Requires=mysql.service/d; /^After=mysql.service/d' /etc/systemd/system/isupipe-go.service` plus maybe add `After=network-online.target`/`Wants=network-online.target`. Could just remove lines. Then `systemctl daemon-reload`. Stop/disable mysql, pdns on s3 to free resources:
```
sudo systemctl disable --now mysql pdns
```
But be careful app unit may have `After=mysql` removed. Good. On s3 MySQL may be used by nothing else. We'll keep nginx.
Nginx config: copy our file to sites-enabled, move backup out. Ensure config upstream. reload.
Then test app on s3 via s1 curl with `--resolve test001.u.isucon.dev:443:10.0.1.76` (s1 can reach s3:443 allowed). It may connect through proxy on s1? Use unset proxies. Test login. Also test register on s3 (creates DNS record in s1) and DNS query. But registering via s3 with host test001 maybe new user, then DNS record points s3 due env; test from s1. Fine.

Let's deploy s3.

{"command":"ssh s3 'cp -a /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe.orig 2>/dev/null || true; cp -a /home/isucon/env.sh /home/isucon/env.sh.orig 2>/dev/null || true'
cd /work/webapp/go && tar czf - *.go go.mod go.sum | ssh s3 'cd /home/isucon/webapp/go && tar xzf -'
scp -q /work/webapp/go/isupipe s3:/tmp/isupipe.new
scp -q /tmp/isupipe.conf s3:/tmp/isupipe.conf
ssh s3 'sudo systemctl stop isupipe-go; sudo mv /tmp/isupipe.new /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe; sudo chown isucon:isucon /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe
sudo cp -a /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/isupipe.conf /etc/nginx/isupipe.conf.orig 2>/dev/null || true; sudo cp /tmp/isupipe.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/isupipe.conf; sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/*.orig; sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo cp -a /etc/systemd/system/isupipe-go.service /etc/systemd/system/isupipe-go.service.orig; sudo sed -i "/^Requires=mysql.service/d; /^After=mysql.service/d" /etc/systemd/system/isupipe-go.service; sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo tee /home/isucon/env.sh >/dev/null <<EOF
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_NET=\"tcp\"
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_ADDRESS=\"10.0.1.56\"
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_PORT=\"3306\"
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_USER=\"isucon\"
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_DATABASE=\"isupipe\"
ISUCON13_MYSQL_DIALCONFIG_PARSETIME=\"true\"
ISUCON13_POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS=\"10.0.1.76\"
ISUCON13_POWERDNS_DISABLED=\"false\"
ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS=\"10.0.1.89\"
EOF
sudo systemctl disable --now mysql pdns >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
sudo systemctl start isupipe-go; sleep 1; systemctl is-active isupipe-go nginx; sudo ss -lntp | grep -E ":(80|443|8080|3306|53) " | head -20
cat /home/isucon/env.sh'","description":"Deploy app and nginx to s3 as second app tier"}

import re, sys, zlib
path, primary, secondary = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
keep = {"pipe", "ns1", "u.isucon.dev", "test001"}

PY

Critical: s3 was IDLE during run! Its app CPU 0, no traffic. DNS split records point s3, but benchmark traffic still all hit s1? Why? Maybe benchmark caches DNS resolution results or uses `pipe.u.isucon.dev` for all requests? The warnings show hosts moririka0.u.isucon.dev etc; the benchmark probably resolves but perhaps DNS response from s1 still returns s1 for those names? Our split counts only records in DB; but PowerDNS might be serving stale zone from `cache-ttl=0`? We set cache 0. Or maybe benchmark's DNS resolver caches addresses from before init? Or it uses a fixed mapping / uses `pipe` IP for all? Wait s3 saw zero traffic, while 751 records point s3. The benchmark likely uses `--dns-server` s1 but maybe it resolves all names at start before initialize? It may build users from initial data and use IP? Actually it may resolve names through DNS but perhaps the zone split didn't take effect because `init_zone.sh` didn't actually update s1 DB? It did: DB counts show 751 s3. But PowerDNS might still have old zone cached because `pdnsutil load-zone` with `cache-ttl=0` and no restart? PowerDNS caches authoritative zone data? We set `zone-cache-refresh-interval=0`, `zone-metadata-cache-ttl=0`. Should re-read. But maybe PDNS process keeps a *domain* in-memory cache with records loaded at startup? It queries backend per request normally. Yet we saw after manual init raw DNS for `www` and initial users returned s3. So DNS serves split. Then why no traffic to s3? Maybe the benchmark connects to IP obtained via DNS *before* benchmark initialization? It may resolve all `*.u.isucon.dev` names during static check before initialize? The output "静的ファイルチェック" before initialize; maybe it resolves then. But zone records before our manual init were also split? We manually initialized just before run 5, so yes split. Unless benchmark's DNS resolver caches results from run 4 (before split) and doesn't honor TTL=0? It might use Go's net resolver which caches? Go resolver doesn't cache. The benchmarker might have a custom DNS cache with fixed TTL. It uses names maybe resolved once at startup and reused across runs? But it runs as separate process per benchmark invocation? The bench wrapper sends to long-running benchmarker maybe process persists? Could cache DNS across runs in memory; then run 5 used addresses from run 4 (all s1). The log says "名前解決を行う対象のサーバー" selected s1; maybe benchmarker process runs per job but could be persistent server with in-memory DNS cache. If it caches name->IP at startup before run 4 and never updates, split won't work. But then future runs would continue s1, making s3 useless. We need determine. Could modify `pipe.u.isucon.dev` A record to point to s3 or load balance at connection level? Hmm.

Alternative way to use s3 without DNS split: run a TCP-level load balancer on s1 that forwards some connections to s3, while DNS user records still point s1. But s1 nginx receives connections; we can configure nginx `upstream` with s1 app and s3 app, load balance at HTTP request level. That would distribute app CPU to s3 while s1 still handles TLS/nginx/PDNS. The app traffic from nginx can be proxied to s1 or s3 backends. This bypasses DNS split requirement and works even if DNS all s1. We can set nginx upstream on s1:
```
upstream isupipe_backend {
  server 127.0.0.1:8080;
  server 10.0.1.76:8080;
  keepalive 256;
}

Moving DB definitely offloads CPU regardless of query pattern, at cost of network. We can also set negative cache 10 with purge/expiration to reduce remote DB load. But new user records immediate: negative cache for a not-yet-existing name could be cached; after registration, if we call purge via HTTP API, safe. We can implement purge using PDNS HTTP API. Or set negative cache small e.g. 2s; benchmark might register then resolve within 2s and get NXDOMAIN if name was queried just before. Risk. Better purge.

Actually, if we move DB remote, s2 MySQL can handle unique DNS queries with indexes; network latency maybe 0.2ms -> 5000 QPS, likely enough. The DNS water torture parallelism 13 maybe ~13k QPS? Could be high but s2 MySQL can do tens of thousands simple queries. Let's move.

Then adjust nginx pipe routing and weights. We can do both before run 7. But we want measure each change effect; with 9 runs left, we can do combined and then further tune. Let's implement:
- Move isudns to s2.
- On s1 app, update DNS_DB_ADDRESS to s2 and restart.
- PDNS remote.
- Nginx pipe server: initialize local, all other /api to hash upstream. Increase s3 weight maybe 2. But need ensure pipe `/api/register` on s3 uses DNS_DB_ADDRESS s2 (update s3 env), powerDNSSubdomainAddress s3. Then new users point s3; s3 nginx must handle DNS wildcard. Currently s3 nginx config uses upstream local and server block for wildcard; yes. But we stopped s3 pdns/mysql; s3 nginx running. New user subdomain DNS points s3 IP; s3 nginx serves local app. Good. But s1 nginx `pipe` server /api excluding initialize will hash pipe requests between s1/s3 based on `$host` (always pipe), meaning consistent hash maps pipe to one backend deterministically! If we use the same hash upstream for pipe with host `pipe`, all pipe requests would go to whichever backend hash selects. We need a separate upstream for pipe that load-balances requests round-robin between s1/s3 (except initialize local). Use `upstream isupipe_pipe { server 127.0.0.1:8080; server 10.0.1.76:8080; keepalive 256; }` default round-robin. Then pipe registration/login/search spread across both per request. But registration on s3 new records point s3; new user host hash may map s3 or s1; okay. However session cookies are same. Initialize exact local.
- For wildcard hosts, use hash upstream with weights. Set s3 weight=2? Need check nginx consistent hash weights. We can set `server 127.0.0.1:8080 weight=1; server 10.0.1.76:8080 weight=2;` and test distribution sample. Since s3 app CPU idle 86%, send ~2/3. But pipe round-robin also sends half pipe to s3. Combined s3 load maybe ~50-60%, s1 ~40%. Good.
- But if pipe registration hits s3, new user record points s3 IP (10.0.1.76). Then DNS for that user goes directly to s3 nginx, bypassing s1 nginx hash, so all that user's traffic hits local s3 app. This creates skew: new users (maybe 200) all s3 if registration requests happen to hit s3 half the time; records point s3 for those. s3 can handle. Fine.
- If pipe register hits s1, new record points s1, but subsequent host requests go through s1 nginx hash and may go s3. Fine.
- `POST /api/icon` on pipe? Benchmark icons may be uploaded via user subdomain, not pipe. If via pipe, s3 registration etc. Fine.
- `initialize` must always local s1 and not load-balanced. Use `location = /api/initialize { proxy_pass http://isupipe_primary; ... }` before `location /api`.
- Other pipe endpoints include static? fine.
- Need perhaps keep `GET /api/user/.../icon` on s3? yes.

- Cross-cache invalidation: pipe requests can go to either app; user cache consistency for icons handled. Initialize on s1 clears s3 via peer. Good.
- NG words: host hash sticky for wildcard hosts, so comments/moderate on same streamer host -> same app. But what if pipe endpoints call moderate? Moderate URL is streamer subdomain, so sticky. Good.

Potential issue: `ISUCON13_POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS` on s1/s3 means registrations create records pointing to app server's IP, not nginx? Both app servers have nginx on 443. s3 nginx local app; s1 nginx hash. Good.

Potential issue: s3 app's DNS DB remote s2; `addDNSRecord` inserts record with content s3 IP. s3 nginx TLS cert same, works. s3 app peer URL s1:8080, fine.

Potential issue: s3 nginx after reboot: we disabled s3 pdns/mysql, but nginx enabled. Good.
- s1 PDNS uses s2 DB remote; after reboot, s2 MySQL starts, s1 PDNS may start before s2 ready and fail, then restart (pdns service auto-restart). Good, eventually. Could add `After=network-online` but not necessary; pdns restart policy? It restarted earlier. Yes.

Let's implement isudns move carefully:
1. Dump isudns on s1 (after current all-s1 data).
2. On s2, drop/create/import. Need stop s2? It's live but benchmark not running; app maybe no traffic. Dropping isudns only affects PDNS if it uses remote after; currently s1 PDNS local, so no impact. s2 isupipe unaffected.
3. Update s1 pdns gmysql-host conf to 10.0.1.56. Test `pdnsutil list-all-zones` from s1 hits remote. Restart pdns, test DNS raw. Ensure query works.
4. Update s1 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.56, s3 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.56, maybe also ISUCON13_POWERDNS_SUBDOMAIN_ADDRESS on s1 remains 10.0.1.89, s3 10.0.1.76. Restart s1/s3 apps to pick env. This will clear caches? Restart does. Fine.
5. Update s1 nginx config with pipe round-robin and exact initialize local, wildcard hash s3 weight 2. Need keep pipe `/api/initialize` local. Also maybe pipe `/api/static`? only init.
6. Manual initialize via pipe -> s1 local; zone loads into remote s2; all records point s1 because secondary env removed. New records from test register maybe s1/s3 depending. Then test routing headers: pipe /api/tag should alternate backends (round-robin) maybe we can send multiple requests and see X-Upstream; pipe initialize local. Wildcard sample mostly s3.
7. Test s3 direct DNS registration if pipe goes s3; not necessary but maybe send register to pipe multiple times and see header; if s3, check DNS record points s3 and resolves. We can test with a unique name.
8. Run bench #7 with monitoring.

Before doing all, consider keeping local MySQL running on s1 idle; PDNS remote. App dnsConn remote s2. The s1 local MySQL still has isudns but unused. Its CPU should drop to ~0. Could even stop it later but `Requires` service issue. Leave.

Use dump includes CREATE TABLE and data, no CREATE DATABASE if not --databases. We'll create database, then import. Then `GRANT ALL` (existing). Test `pdnsutil list-all-zones` after config change. content.text:
Current weight 1:2 yields 58% s3, not 67%, but okay. s3 CPU in run6 was 15% with weight 1:1 (probably ~50% hosts) and s1 app 50%. Maybe s3 got fewer due hot host skew. We want s3 to take more, perhaps weight 1:4 (80% s3) to exploit idle. But s3 app CPU was 15% with ~50% hosts, so doubling to 80% -> ~24%, still low. s1 app 50% at ~50% hosts -> with 20% hosts maybe 20%. That could reduce s1 app CPU by 30% of a core. Combined with moving MySQL off s1, s1 idle should rise. Let's set s3 weight=5 or 6. Test distribution sample after reload. Weight 1:5 maybe gives 80-85% s3. We'll set s1 weight=1, s3 weight=5. But caution: if s3 app can't handle 80% plus pipe 50%, its CPU maybe 30-40%, still fine. s3 also could receive new user DNS direct; okay.

Also note s1 app CPU includes `notifyPeer`? No. s3 app maybe not warming caches? It gets per-run initialize clear, then loads as needed.

Now run bench #7 with moved DNS DB, pipe LB, wildcard weight 1:5. Adjust nginx weight before run. Also maybe we should stop s3 nginx? Not necessary (idle). s3 pdns/mysql stopped already; good.

Set weight=5. Reload. Test distribution maybe 80. Then run bench #7 monitoring. Let's update.

Run 7: s1 idle 40%, s3 idle 51%, s2 idle 21% (MySQL 130% of one core, total s2 CPU us 58% across 2 cores -> ~1.16 cores). Now s2 is the bottleneck-ish: MySQL uses 130% of one core (top % is relative to one core? top shows 129.7% for mysqld, meaning 1.3 cores). s2 total idle 21%. We have s2 doing both isupipe and DNS; MySQL CPU high. s1 improved. s3 has headroom ~50%. Could move some MySQL load or tune further.

Score 333k. To improve, we need reduce MySQL CPU/query count or add more DB capacity. Query counts per 60s: Questions 655k, Queries 1.62M (includes multi? Queries includes stored? Com_select 403k, Com_insert 180k, Com_delete 42k). That's ~10k QPS, high. MySQL CPU 1.3 cores; s2 has 2 cores. Could optimize queries/indices, or use s3 for read replica? Maybe.

Notable Com_delete 42k: Why so many deletes? `moderateHandler` deletes old livecomments for each ngword (maybe many). Com_insert 180k: livecomments/reactions etc. Com_select 403k. We can reduce DB queries in hot paths.

Current app caches reduce many reads, but hot write paths still do:
- `postLivecomment`: getLivestreamEntry cache (should hit), getNGWords cache (should hit), INSERT one row. No selects. Insert 1.
- `postReaction`: getLivestreamEntry cache, INSERT 1.
- `getLivecomments`/`getReactions`: SELECT rows each poll (many). Benchmark polls timeline frequently. These cause Com_select high and possibly large `Handler_read_next`.
- `getIcon` on cache hit no DB.
- `enter/exit`: INSERT/DELETE one.
- `moderate`: INSERT ngword + multiple DELETE livecomments (maybe ~? 42k deletes from moderation; benchmark may moderate often).
- Stats/payment maybe few.
- Login/register initial: many inserts/selects.

Could reduce MySQL CPU by:
1. Tune MySQL further: buffer pool 2GB already, no disk reads. CPU is query execution. Increase `innodb_buffer_pool_instances` (currently default 8? with 2GB maybe 8), `innodb_thread_concurrency` default 0. CPU 130% on 2 cores; maybe not fully saturated. Could set `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=0`, done. `innodb_doublewrite=OFF`, done. `skip-log-bin`, done. `performance_schema=OFF`, done. Query cache removed in MySQL 8. Could set `innodb_autoinc_lock_mode=2`, default. `innodb_spin_wait_delay` etc not huge.
2. Add/optimize indexes. Already many. `Com_delete` might do full scans on livecomments by `livestream_id` index (good), but delete uses `comment LIKE` no index; scans comments per stream. If many comments, moderate deletes many rows. Could change moderate deletion to use in-memory check? But data must be deleted from DB for final consistency. The benchmark may expect old spam comments removed. Could batch delete only matching comments using `LIKE` on index; okay. 42k deletes means many rows deleted. Could be because `moderate` loops over all ngwords for livestream, and initial ng_words per stream maybe many? Wait initial_ngwords has 14k rows across 7500 streams (~2 each). When a streamer moderates a new word, our code fetches all words (initial ~2 + new) and executes DELETE for each; if benchmark adds many ngwords over time, count grows. Original also loops all. If moderate called for each new word, and words accumulate, deletes O(n). But 42k deletes / 60s suggests many livecomments deleted, maybe because initial/spam comments generated. Could be okay.

3. Use s3 as MySQL read replica? We could run second MySQL on s3 with read-only replica of s2, route read-only API (get livecomments, reactions, search, stats) to s3, offloading s2. But replication setup and consistency could be tricky; benchmark writes then immediately reads own comments, replication lag could cause failures. Not ideal.

4. Split the database: use s2 for writes and s3 for reads with asynchronous replication, but same consistency risk. Could route only low-consistency endpoints (search/tag/stats?) to s3. But stats need current writes. Not worth.

5. Use s3's local MySQL for DNS instead of s2, so s2 only isupipe. We moved isudns to s2; that adds DNS query load to s2. But s3 currently has MySQL stopped and CPU idle; we could move isudns to s3 instead! Then s2 only app DB, s1 PDNS queries s3. This would offload DNS queries from s2 to s3, which has ~50% idle. But s3 also handles app traffic (current s3 app 80% CPU? top shows 91% of one core, s3 total CPU us 38% across 2 cores = 0.76 cores; idle 46%). Adding DNS DB load (MySQL on s3) might use ~? s1 local MySQL was 60% of one core for DNS before moving; but now s2 MySQL total 130% includes both isupipe and isudns. Isudns may be a significant part. Moving to s3 could balance. But s3 has app + nginx + mysql; 2 cores; current idle ~46% total, enough for 0.6 core DNS? Maybe. Alternatively move DNS DB back to s1? s1 now idle 40%, local MySQL would use ~0.6 core, s1 idle maybe 10%; s2 would drop to ~? but s1 currently also PDNS 34% and nginx; s1 total us 31.7% over 2 cores ~0.63 core, idle 40% (0.8 core). Adding 0.6 core might saturate s1. Not good.
   Move isudns to s3: s3 current idle 0.92 core; DNS MySQL 0.6 core could fit but tight when app load high. Maybe better to optimize DNS query load first: set negative cache >0 with purge on registration, or serve DNS from a local backend on s1.

Let's understand how much of s2 MySQL CPU is DNS vs isupipe. We can measure by temporarily stopping? Can't easily separate. We could check MySQL `performance_schema` disabled; could enable and use `events_statements_summary_by_digest` for one run, but adds overhead; we have 8 runs and can use one diagnostic with performance_schema ON and query digest after run. Or use `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS` `Com_select` on s2 includes isupipe. To estimate DNS queries, PDNS query log disabled; can count MySQL `Com_select` from isudns by `performance_schema` or enable general log briefly. But maybe simpler: check PowerDNS stats via `pdns_control show *`? It may report query counts. PDNS has `pdns_control show *`? Commands: `pdns_control show <statistic>` maybe. Not sure. We can use `pdns_control list`? Or `rec_control` only recursor. Could enable `log-dns-queries` for one run but log huge. Instead use tcpdump? Not needed.

Alternative test: run a local synthetic DNS query load from s1 to s1 PDNS and see s2 MySQL CPU increase; but app load not. We can measure query latency. Not necessary.

6. Increase use of s3 app further: s3 idle 51%, s1 idle 40%. We could shift more app to s3 (weight 10 or route pipe fully to hash) until s3 CPU ~80%. But if s2 MySQL is bottleneck, pushing app harder may not increase score much; however s3 still has headroom and s1 has headroom. The benchmark may not be saturating because of per-request latency from MySQL. More app concurrency won't help if DB maxed. But s2 idle 21% not zero, so maybe latency/queue not fully. We can try shift more to s3 and see score. A run costs; we can combine with DNS DB move to s3 and app weight increase.

7. Optimize app DB queries to reduce s2 load. Let's inspect hot endpoint counts during run 7. We can enable nginx access log on s1/s3 for run 8 to get endpoint request counts and upstream times. But run 8 also test changes. We can enable access log with `$request_time` now and leave for run 8; it adds overhead but gives data. Alternatively app can expose counters via /internal/metrics; too much. Nginx access log on s1 for all API (including proxied s3) and on s3 direct (if any) would show request counts. Since all traffic enters s1 nginx (DNS all s1), s1 access log covers all requests; even proxied to s3. We can log only API with request time to /var/log/nginx/api.log. That gives counts and upstream response times. Disk writes ~ maybe 1M requests? Run 7 score 333k, viewers 1709, requests maybe hundreds of thousands. Logging could be heavy on s1 (already 40% idle) but maybe okay. We can use `access_log /var/log/nginx/api.log` with buffered to reduce overhead (`buffer=64k flush=5s`). Nginx access_log supports buffer. Use custom format with `$request_time $upstream_response_time`. Enable on s1 for both pipe/wildcard. Then run 8 perhaps with combined changes. After analyze, disable. This is useful.

8. MySQL query optimization:
- `getLivecomments` query `SELECT * FROM livecomments WHERE livestream_id=? ORDER BY created_at DESC [LIMIT]` with index (livestream_id, created_at) good. It fetches all comments maybe hundreds; returns full nested objects from cache. Good.
- `getReactions` similar.
- `searchLivestreams` with `limit=50` uses PK order id desc limit 50 (good) then load tags for 50; cache might already have them. `search?tag=...` uses `livestream_tags WHERE tag_id=? ORDER BY livestream_id DESC` with index (tag_id,livestream_id) good, returns maybe thousands? For popular tags could be many rows; original returns all. Could be heavy but 44 requests/run, not huge.
- `getMyLivestreams` user_id index good.
- `getIcon` cache mostly no DB; after init, first icon for each user queries users/themes/icons (batch). 1000 users, okay.
- Stats ranking queries may be heavy: user stats ~10 requests, each scans/joins; livestream stats ~2 requests. Not main.
- `register`: insert user/theme, DNS insert; ~200, not main.
- `postLivecomment` insert only. `getLivestreamEntry` cache for active streams should hit after first. But note `pipe` round-robin sends register/login/search requests to both apps, each has separate cache. For wildcard hosts, sticky hash, good.
- `moderate`: DELETE and INSERT. Com_delete 42k huge. Maybe because our moderate delete runs for all ngwords and deletes many old comments. Could optimize to one delete per new word only? Original behavior deletes past comments matching *all* ngwords for livestream, but after first moderate, old comments already deleted; re-running all words on each moderate is redundant for words previously applied. We can track which ngwords have been applied in a set/cache and only delete for newly added word. That would reduce deletes dramatically. Need preserve semantics: when adding a new NG word, delete past comments matching new word. All previous words were already applied at the time they were added (or initial words? Initial ng_words from seed maybe none for active streams; but on first moderate, original deletes comments matching all existing words, including seed NG words. Our cache loads all words; we can on first moderate of a livestream apply all cached words, then mark them applied. On subsequent moderates, only apply the new word. This preserves eventual removal (any old comment matching an old word was already deleted when that word was added; if comments were inserted before old word was added and not deleted because cache? We apply all on first). Need be careful concurrent moderate; benchmark likely sequential per stream. Implement `appliedNG map[int64]map[int64]bool` or per-livestream set of word IDs applied. On moderate, after inserting new word and getting all words, determine words to apply: if no applied set for livestream, apply all words (including new); else apply only new word. Mark all applied. On initialize clear. This could cut Com_delete from 42k to maybe much lower. But is Com_delete actually from moderate? Could also be `exitLivestreamHandler` deletes viewer history; benchmark many enter/exit. 1709 viewers * maybe 1 enter/exit = ~3.4k deletes. 42k much larger, likely moderation deletes. Also `DELETE FROM livestream_viewers_history` maybe repeated; could be ~? not 42k. Could track with logs. But optimizing moderate is worthwhile.
- `moderate` also inserts many NG words? Com_insert 180k includes comments/reactions/viewer history/users etc.
- `livecomments` deletion by moderation removes spam comments; score maybe tips unaffected. But DB CPU.
- Could we avoid deleting old comments entirely, since final consistency check perhaps only checks reports/stats? The benchmark might verify moderated comments are gone via GET livecomments, so need delete. But only new word's matches. Our optimization safe.

- `enterLivestreamHandler` inserts every enter; benchmark viewers may enter/exit repeatedly; Com_insert 180k includes many. Could use `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`? No unique index. Could skip inserting if already exists? Original inserts each. Benchmark may verify viewer count? It increments. Not sure. Could add unique index? Might break expected counts. Leave.

- `postReaction`/`postLivecomment` response building with full nested livestream object is huge JSON (1KB) but CPU mostly app, not DB. s3/s1 have headroom.

- `getLivestreamStatistics` ranking query computes all 7500 scores every request; maybe benchmark calls frequently? Run 4 logs only 2. Not main.

9. Could add a write batching / async? Not necessary.

10. Could use MySQL `UNIX socket` or local DB on s1? s2 remote app queries add network overhead but not CPU. s2 CPU high; maybe move app DB to s1? s1 currently less loaded but would add local MySQL isupipe CPU, maybe balance. Actually s1 has idle 40%, s3 idle 51%, s2 only 21%. We could run a second MySQL replica/partition? Or just move isupipe DB to s1? Initially app+DB on s1 had high CPU because both app and DB on same 2 cores; now with app split s1 maybe could host DB? But remote app from s3 would go to s1 DB; s1 already nginx+pdns+app. s2 would be idle. We could balance by running MySQL on s1 and s3? Data consistency. Could use s1 as primary and s2 as read replica? Not.

Could use s2 plus s3 both as database servers with different tables? Sharding by user/livestream? Too complex. Or use s3 local MySQL as read replica for DNS only (move isudns) to offload s2. That's easy and likely helps ~0.2-0.4 core. Let's do that: move isudns DB to s3 (instead of s2). Then s2 only isupipe. s3 runs MySQL for DNS; s1 PDNS connects s3; s2 app DB unchanged. s3 currently app CPU ~0.76 core; add DNS MySQL maybe 0.3 core, total ~1.1 core out of 2, still okay. s2 frees maybe 0.3-0.5 core. This could improve score. We already have dump on s2; can dump from s2 or copy original /tmp/isudns.sql via workspace. Better dump current isudns from s2 after run7 (same schema) and import to s3. Then update s1 pdns gmysql-host to 10.0.1.76; update s1/s3 app DNS_DB_ADDRESS to 10.0.1.76. Need start/configure s3 MySQL (currently stopped/disabled, config original bind 127.0.0.1, buffer pool 128M). We can enable and configure bind 0.0.0.0, buffer pool maybe 512M, skip-log-bin, etc. s3 memory 3.6GB, app uses ~230MB, okay. Then grant isudns@'%' and isudns@'127.0.0.1'? PDNS on s1 connects remote 10.0.1.76 -> user isudns@'%' matches. Start mysql on s3; it was originally configured with isupipe DB too but we can leave. However s3 app service requires mysql removed earlier; starting mysql no issue. We should ensure MySQL on s3 is enabled to start on reboot (systemctl enable mysql). We disabled it earlier; enable now.
- Note s3's local isudns database originally may still exist and be stale from initial; we'll drop/create/import current.
- s3 MySQL port 3306 listens 0.0.0.0; s3 app connects s2 for isupipe; no conflict.
- Security group allows s1->s3:3306 (test).
- After moving, PDNS queries s3; s1 no local MySQL CPU already 0 (idle). s2 MySQL CPU should drop by DNS portion. We can measure run8.
- Alternatively move isudns back to s1 local and turn on negative caching; but s1 CPU. Moving to s3 uses idle capacity better.

On s3 configure MySQL and import. Then update s1 PDNS and env; update s3 env; restart both apps with new binary. Let's perform.

1. Dump s2 isudns to /tmp/isudns2.sql via ssh s2 (as root).
2. scp to s3.
3. Configure s3 MySQL zz file, start/enable, create DB/user, import.
4. Test s1 -> s3:3306.
5. Update s1 pdns host to s3, restart pdns, test DNS.
6. Update s1 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.76; s3 env same; restart apps with new binary.
7. Update nginx access log config and reload.

Let's do step by step with careful output.

Import still has split counts because s2 isudns was from before we reinitialized? We reinitialized all s1 on s1 local, then moved dump to s2 before that? Let's timeline: We moved isudns to s2 by dumping s1 after all-s1 manual init at 12:20. That dump had 2356 records 2354 s1. Then s2 isudns imported. We haven't run benchmark init after moving? Run 7 benchmark initialized through s1 with PDNS remote s2: init_zone.sh loaded zone all s1 into s2 isudns, then registrations during run7 added new records (some s3 IP, because pipe LB to s3 registrations with s3 env). So s2 isudns after run7 has 2638 records: 1972 s1, 664 s3 (new users from run7 registration via s3). That's fine; dump to s3 includes this state. New benchmark initialize on run8 will load zone all s1 (clearing records) and then new registrations. But note zone file load may not delete old records? `pdnsutil load-zone` replaces zone records, likely deletes all old records and inserts zone. Yes. So split old records will be cleared. Good.

Now update s1 pdns host to s3, restart, test. Update env DNS_DB on s1/s3, deploy new binaries, restart apps. Then nginx access log. Let's do.

content.name: bash
content.arguments:
{"command":"ssh s1 'sudo sed -i "s/^gmysql-host=.*/gmysql-host=10.0.1.76/" /etc/powerdns/pdns.d/gmysql-host.conf; cat /etc/powerdns/pdns.d/gmysql-host.conf; sudo systemctl restart pdns; sleep 2; systemctl is-active pdns; sudo pdnsutil list-all-zones
sudo sed -i "s|^ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS=.*|ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS=\"10.0.1.76\"|" /home/isucon/env.sh; grep DNS_DB /home/isucon/env.sh
python3 - <<PY
import socket,struct,random
name="pipe.u.isucon.dev"; tid=random.randrange(65536); hdr=struct.pack(">HHHHHH",tid,0x0100,1,0,0,0)
body=b"".join(bytes([len(x)])+x.encode() for x in name.split("."))+b"\0"+struct.pack(">HH",1,1)
s=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM); s.settimeout(2); s.sendto(hdr+body,("127.0.0.1",53)); d,_=s.recvfrom(4096)
print("dns",name,"rcode",d[3]&15,"ip",socket.inet_ntoa(d[-4:]))
PY'
ssh s3 'sudo sed -i "s|^ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS=.*|ISUCON13_DNS_DB_ADDRESS=\"10.0.1.76\"|" /home/isucon/env.sh; grep DNS_DB /home/isucon/env.sh'
# deploy new binaries
scp -q /work/webapp/go/isupipe s1:/tmp/isupipe.new
scp -q /work/webapp/go/isupipe s3:/tmp/isupipe.new
ssh s1 'sudo systemctl stop isupipe-go; sudo mv /tmp/isupipe.new /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe; sudo chown isucon:isucon /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe; sudo systemctl start isupipe-go'
ssh s3 'sudo systemctl stop isupipe-go; sudo mv /tmp/isupipe.new /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe; sudo chown isucon:isucon /home/isucon/webapp/go/isupipe; sudo systemctl start isupipe-go'
sleep 2
ssh s1 'systemctl is-active isupipe-go pdns nginx'; ssh s3 'systemctl is-active isupipe-go nginx mysql'","description":"Move DNS DB to s3 and deploy new app binaries"}

content.text:
Run9 score 325,788, similar to run8 323,039, slightly higher but below run7 333,473. There were 2 "expected 201 actual 400" general errors (moderated spam?) likely okay per docs says general error not penalty? The docs mention a specific general error for moderated spam expected 400 actual 201 is not penalty. Here expected 201 actual 400 means a comment was rejected as spam when benchmark expected success, causing viewer departure. That's potentially due our NG word cache/check bug or benchmark posting comments containing moderator words that shouldn't be filtered? The docs caution about expected 400 actual 201 being ignored. Expected 201 actual 400 is a real issue: Our NG word matching may be over-filtering compared to original. Could be because our cached NG words for livestream include words from previous state/run? We clear caches on initialize. Or because our moderation applies/deletes more? Wait postLivecomment checks `ngword.UserID == livestream.Model.UserID` and `contains(comment, word)`. Original SQL checks all ngwords for livestream owner, same. But our `isNGWord` uses exact case-sensitive substring; original SQL LIKE may be case-insensitive? If ngword "Go" and comment "go", original might filter (case-insensitive) while ours doesn't; that would produce expected 400 actual 201, not expected 201 actual 400. Our over-filtering could happen if original LIKE pattern treats `%` or `_` wildcards in ngword; ours literal. If ngword contains `_`, original would wildcard match more, ours less. So ours should not over-filter relative to original, except maybe collation differences (ours exact vs original case-insensitive) -> less filtering. So 201 vs 400 expected not from NG words? Wait expected 201 actual 400 means benchmark posted a comment it expected to be accepted, but our app rejected as spam. That over-filtering could be due **stale NG cache** containing words from *other livestreams*? `getNGWordsForLivestream` caches by livestreamID. Clear at init. During run, moderate inserts words for specific livestream. Could a livestream ID be reused? New streams IDs unique. No.

Could be due our `moderate` first-pass applying all words including initial ngwords and then deleting comments, but that doesn't affect post filter.

Maybe the expected 201 comment was posted by a viewer to a stream where the streamer had added an NG word that is a substring of a legitimate comment. Benchmark might generate comments containing NG words deliberately, and expects either 400 if "spam" or 201 for normal. It knows which comments contain spam? The error might be because our NG word cache includes **new words added by benchmark's moderation in a different app instance**? With pipe round-robin and host sticky, moderate for a livestream goes to same host (streamer domain) -> same backend. But what if a livestream is owned by a user whose host is not the same as the URL host used to moderate? The benchmark may send moderate request to `pipe` or to streamer's domain? It likely uses streamer's domain. If it uses a different host (e.g., viewer domain?) then our host hash could route to a different app with stale NG cache; but moderate inserts DB, other app cache old; a subsequent comment on streamer host app could miss the new NG word (expected 400 actual 201), not over-filter.
Over-filtering could be because we apply NG words from *all users*? In `isNGWord` loop, we check ngword.UserID == livestream.Model.UserID. Good.

Wait initial `getNgwords` handler filters by session user, but postLivecomment original checks `WHERE user_id = livestreamModel.UserID AND livestream_id` (owner). Our cache loads all words for livestream, and we filter owner. Good.

Maybe our string `contains` is treating empty? We guard len>0. Good.

Could the 400 actually be from another validation? postLivecomment only 400 for malformed JSON or spam; benchmark sent valid JSON, so spam. Maybe benchmark's expected 201 comment contains an NG word that original implementation would also reject, but benchmark expected 201 because that word was added by moderation to a *different* livestream but our cache keyed by livestream ID? Could duplicate livestream IDs? No.

Maybe NG word cache from prior run not cleared on s3? We do initialize on s1 notifyPeer clear s3. But does notifyPeer work after app restarts? s1 peer URL points s3; s3 peer URL points s1. We tested. If s3 clear didn't happen, s3 could have stale NG words from previous run for livestream IDs that are reused in new run. Initial livestream IDs are same, but benchmark-created livestream IDs start at 7500 every run. If s3 cache for a new stream ID from previous run remains, and new run creates a new stream with *same ID* but different owner/words, then postLivecomment on s3 for that livestream could use stale NG words from previous run, over-filtering. This is likely! Our clear notification should prevent, but maybe it failed in run9? Let's verify s1->s3 clear works (we tested manually via curl with header, got 204). The initializeHandler calls notifyPeer after local clear and init. But we restructured routes: `/internal/clear-cache` is registered where? We moved route registration section; we inserted internal routes before "// 初期化" in main earlier. When we rewrote routes from `start=s.index('\t// 初期化\n')`, did we preserve internal routes? Let's check main. The internal routes were before `// 初期化`, so our replacement start at `// 初期化` kept them. Good.
But we removed global session middleware and put session only on group; internal routes are not in group, no session needed. Good.
`notifyPeer` uses `ISUCON13_PEER_URL` from s1 env; after we restarted s1 app, env still has peer URL? Yes we appended and restarted before. But wait when we changed s1 env to DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.76, we restarted s1 app after; peer URL preserved. Good.
Could `initializeHandler` call notifyPeer before s3 app is ready? It is ready. Manual init smoke after run9? We can check s3 cache clearing by adding a debug endpoint to report cache size? Not now. We can test by making a moderate word on s3, then call initialize and see if post comment gets accepted. We could write a test. But likely clear works.

Another possibility: Our `addNGWordToCache` logic has a bug: When first moderate on a livestream, `getNGWordsForLivestream` loads old words from DB and caches. Then `addNGWordToCache` prepends new word. But `words` variable points to old slice (without new). We build toApply old + new. Fine. On subsequent moderate, `getNGWordsForLivestream` returns cache including new. `addNGWordToCache` prepends new. `applied` exists. We only apply new. Fine.
But `applied` map is keyed by livestreamID, not cleared between runs? clearCaches clears `ngApplied`. But if s3 clear fails, stale applied could cause not deleting new word's old comments, not over-filtering.

Over-filtering (400) could be due **we filter against NG words whose `UserID` matches session/livestream owner but cache has words from same livestream ID from another streamer in a previous run**, because we didn't clear s3 caches. That seems plausible. Let's verify whether s3 clear works by inspecting s3 app cache via an internal debug endpoint? We can add debug endpoint to return len(ngCache), user cache size. But adding code requires deploy; we have 6 runs. Could use `GODEBUG`? No. We can test behavior manually:
1. On s3 backend, choose a livestream host that routes to s3 (e.g., ayamazaki0). Find a livestream owned by a user whose host routes s3? Hard.
2. Add NG word "uniquetestword" to some livestream via moderate on s3.
3. Call pipe initialize (s1) which should clear s3 cache.
4. Post a comment containing "uniquetestword" to that livestream via its host (which routes to s3) with a viewer session; if cache cleared, the word may still be in DB? Initialize resets DB, so livestream IDs/words gone. To test clear, need preserve word across init? Not possible because DB reset removes word. But cache stale would contain word; after init, livestream ID may be reused by initial data (e.g., ID 7496 initial? initial max ~7495; new stream from manual reserve 7496, after init max maybe 7495, so ID 7496 not exist until new reserve). We could:
   - Use livestream ID that exists initial and add NG word via moderate on s3 (but need owner session and host route s3).
   - Call initialize resetting DB; initial livestream same ID exists with no NG word. Then post a comment containing that word to initial livestream via its owner host (route s3) and see if 400 (stale cache) or 201 (cleared).
This is doable but requires finding a stream owned by a user whose host hashes to s3 and owner password. Initial users all password test? Earlier ayamazaki0/test failed maybe because password not test? We can use test001 (host test001 routes s3 according to X-Upstream earlier! Actually test001 mapped to s3 in run8 sample). We can create a new livestream via test001 reservation through pipe; if pipe round-robin goes s1 or s3, doesn't matter. But host test001 resolves/hash to s3; moderate request to test001 host goes s3 backend. Add word to new stream ID 7496. Then initialize resets DB; but ID 7496 not in initial data (max 7495), so cannot post to same ID (404). Use an initial livestream owned by test001? Check if test001 has initial livestream(s). We can query s2 DB for livestreams user_id=1. If test001 owns some initial streams, use one. Then moderate via test001 host (s3) add word. Initialize resets DB but initial stream same ID remains (restored) with no word. Then post comment containing word via test001 host (s3) with test001 session; if stale cache, 400; if cleared, 201. Let's check if test001 owns streams. Query. This test can be done without benchmark runs. If cache clear fails, we need fix.

Also over-filtering could be cross-app cache not cleared on s2? We don't have app on s2. s1/s3 both should clear. s1 clears local; s3 via notify. If s3 clear works, fine.

Let's query test001's livestreams.

Let's find one (e.g., get names mapped s2) and use. Or we can just send requests to s2 via `--resolve test001...:10.0.1.56` directly, but that bypasses s1 nginx and uses s2 nginx, still tests app. We want s2 app DB/DNS. Let's do. Also test DNS raw from s1 for new record. Then run10.

content.text:
s2 became bottleneck (idle 24%, MySQL probably high, app also). So 3-app hurt. Revert to 2-app with s1+s3. Choose DNS DB placement: run7 (DNS on s2) had 333k, run9 (DNS on s3) 326k. Both similar. With 2-app, s2 only DB; adding DNS to s2 in run7 gave high CPU but best score. However run7 had weight5 (s3 77%) and no session skip; s2 DNS+DB. Run9 with DNS on s3 and weight2 had s3 more loaded. We could try 2-app with DNS on s2 and weight maybe 3-4, plus session skip/batch deletes. This may beat run7. We have 5 runs. Let's plan:
- Run11: Revert to 2-app (remove s2 from s1 nginx upstream, s2 app can stay running idle but not used; remove s2 from peer lists? We can leave s2 peer list, but s2 app may receive clear/invalidation; harmless. However s1 initialize would notify s2 too, extra requests; negligible. s2 app is running with caches but no traffic. It might still be in peer list; no issue. We could leave 3-app code/env but remove s2 from upstream. Then s1/s3 only. Pipe round-robin 2 servers, hash weights: choose s1=1, s3=3 or 4. Current DNS DB on s3. To replicate run7 best, move DNS DB back to s2 and use weight 5. But moving back takes time. Alternatively keep DNS on s3, weight 3 (s3 ~65-70%), maybe score similar. Since run9 with weight2 gave 326, weight5 maybe could exceed. s3 with DNS DB was loaded but idle37% in run9; increasing app share to 70% might saturate s3. In run7 DNS on s2 and weight5, s3 app used 49% (idle51), s2 DB used 79% (idle21). So s2 was bottleneck but score 333. If we move DNS to s2 with session skip/batch delete, maybe s2 DB load slightly lower, s3 app more, could improve. I think best bet is run7 config (DNS on s2) + new optimizations + maybe weight 4 (s3 ~70%). Then run11 measure. If >333, keep. If not, run12 can revert DNS to s3 or adjust weights.

Moving DNS DB back to s2:
- Dump current isudns from s3 (after run10, data includes current). Import to s2. We already have isudns DB on s2 from before run7 but may be stale; re-import fresh.
- Update s1 PDNS gmysql-host to 10.0.1.56, restart; update s1/s3/s2 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.56; restart s1/s3 apps (s2 app not used but env). 
- Nginx s1 config: remove s2 from upstream; set hash weights s1=1,s3=4 (to ~70-75%); pipe round-robin only s1/s3. Could use local `/tmp/isupipe-lb2.conf` and sed weight=4. The local lb2 has weight2; set weight=4. Pipe only s1/s3. This is exactly 2-app. Keep access log off. 
- s2 app can be stopped to free CPU/memory since s2 is DB server; stop s2 isupipe-go service. It is currently running our app; not used. Stopping frees ~0.3GB and some CPU. s2 MySQL only. Ensure s2 app not needed for peer clear (s1/s3 peer lists still include s2, but notify will fail silently; fine). We could remove s2 from peer lists to avoid timeout overhead on initialize/icon. Better update s1/s3 `PEER_URLS` to only each other. s2 env irrelevant. Remove s2 from s1/s3 peer lists and restart apps. This avoids extra 500ms if s2 down per icon (icon invalidation would try s2 and timeout, costly!). Actually notifyPeer loops sequential; if s2 app stopped, each postIcon would wait 500ms on s2 before finishing? It notifies s1 peers in order; s1->s3 first then s2? s1 peer list currently s3,s2; after s3 success, s2 connection refused quickly not timeout (host up, port closed -> immediate RST), so okay but still. Remove s2.
- For run11, use DNS on s2, 2-app. Good.

Let's execute revert. Need be careful not to break. Steps:
1. Dump isudns from s3 to s2; import (drop/create) on s2. s2 MySQL active.
2. Update s1 PDNS host to s2; restart pdns; test DNS.
3. Update s1/s3 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.56. Update s1 peer URLS only s3, s3 only s1. Keep s2 app maybe stop.
4. Update s1 nginx to 2-app weight 4. Could create local from lb2 with weight4. Also remove `server 10.0.1.56` if present (lb2 doesn't have it; current s1 config 3app has s2, we'll overwrite with lb2-based config). Good.
5. Stop s2 app service (`systemctl stop isupipe-go` maybe disable to avoid after reboot? After final reboot, s2 app not needed; stopping is fine, but service enabled maybe starts on reboot and uses CPU idle; harmless. Could disable to avoid. We might later need s2 app? Probably not. Disable now maybe. But if we want to test 3-app later, can re-enable. Leave enabled but stopped; on reboot it starts original? It has our binary/env, but not used. Fine.)
6. Deploy? Binaries already latest on s1/s3. Env changes require restart apps. We'll restart s1/s3.
7. Manual init and smoke; then run11.

Let's do.

content.text:
Run11 CPU:
- s1 idle 37, s2 idle 23 (bottleneck), s3 idle 52. So s2 MySQL is bottleneck again with DNS+isupipe. s3 has lots of headroom, s1 some. We could move DNS DB off s2 to s3 and reduce s2 load, but run9 with DNS s3 had s3 idle37 and s2 idle54, score 326. Hmm. In run11 s2 bottleneck due DNS on s2; moving DNS to s3 gives s3 ~24 idle (run8) or 37 (run9?), and s2 43-54 idle. Scores similar. Perhaps the true limiting factor is not CPU but benchmark client concurrency or DB latency. s2 MySQL at 77% used (idle23) might still not be saturated; but could increase latency.

What about splitting DNS DB between s1 local and s2? PDNS can use one backend, not split. Could move DNS DB to s1 local again and use negative/positive cache; s1 idle37 with room; s2 would be only isupipe (idle ~54), s3 app (idle52). Then all three balanced. But s1 local MySQL adds CPU similar to s2 DNS load, using idle37 -> maybe s1 idle ~10-20; still okay. Original run4/5 with DNS local s1 and local MySQL had s1 saturated because app also on s1 with no s3? Actually run5 had app split but DNS split ineffective; s1 had app ~50%, MySQL 63%, PDNS33%, nginx50 => saturated. Now s1 app is only ~25% hosts (weight4) and session skip, so app CPU lower; adding local MySQL DNS could be okay. But PDNS remote/ local? If DNS DB on s1 local, PDNS queries local (faster), MySQL CPU on s1. s2 only isupipe. This might improve latency and balance. However s1 currently handles nginx for all requests (~0.6 core), PDNS (~0.3), app (~0.3); adding MySQL (~0.5) => ~1.7 core out of2, high but may still. s2 idle ~54 (0.9 core), s3 idle52 (1.0 core). s1 would be bottleneck. Let's implement local DNS DB on s1 for run13:
- Move isudns from s2 to s1 local (refresh dump).
- On s1 local MySQL, drop/create/import isudns, grant isudns@'127.0.0.1' and '%' (already). Note s1 local MySQL has `skip-name-resolve`, user isudns@'%' matches 127.0.0.1; also explicit 127 user.
- Update s1 PDNS gmysql-host=127.0.0.1, restart; test.
- Update s1 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1; s3 env DNS_DB_ADDRESS=10.0.1.89 (s3 app registration inserts remote s1, which is fine). s2 app stopped.
- Restart s1/s3 apps to pick env.
- Maybe adjust nginx weight: keep weight4 first, but s1 will be more loaded. Could set weight6 (s3 ~80%) to reduce s1 app load. Since s1 local MySQL adds CPU, shift app to s3 which has headroom. Pipe round-robin can also be biased to s3: change `upstream isupipe_pipe` add `server 127.0.0.1:8080 weight=1; server 10.0.1.76:8080 weight=2;` so pipe 2/3 to s3. That reduces s1 app further. s3 currently 50% used in run12; adding DNS not to s3 (it's on s1), and app share increase might bring s3 to ~65-70. s2 only isupipe ~50%. s1 nginx+PDNS+MySQL maybe 75% with app lower. This could balance and improve.
- But if s1 local MySQL DNS uses more CPU than estimated, s1 saturates. We can monitor run13. If failed/worse, revert to s2 DNS for run14/15.
- Need be careful s1 local MySQL is also running old isupipe DB; idle. We can drop isupipe on s1 to free disk/memory? Not necessary. Buffer pool 512MB. Could tune local MySQL buffer pool for isudns maybe 512M enough. It has performance_schema off, skip binlog. Good.
- After reboot, PDNS on s1 uses local MySQL; s1 MySQL enabled. Good. s2 MySQL still isupipe. s3 MySQL DNS DB now unused, but running; can stop/disable s3 mysql to free CPU/memory? s3 app no longer uses DNS DB (env points s1), so s3 MySQL unused. We can stop/disable s3 mysql, freeing ~0.2 core/1GB and reducing s3 load. Good. But if s3 app registration inserts to s1 DB, no local. Do it.
- s3 currently has MySQL running for DNS; stop/disable before run13. This also means s3 resources for app, good.

Let's do local DNS migration and bias app to s3. Then run13. If score improves, keep for run14/15; if not, revert to run11 config for run14 and final run15.

1. Dump isudns from s2 (current after run12) to workspace, scp to s1, import into s1 local MySQL.

5. Nginx s1: weight s3 maybe 6; pipe upstream s3 weight=2 vs s1=1. Create config from lb2:
   - hash: s1 weight=1, s3 weight=6 (gives ~85%? test sample)
   - pipe: s1 weight=1, s3 weight=2.

6. Manual init, verify DNS local works; sample distribution. Run13 monitors+bench.

{"command":"ssh s1 'set -e
unset https_proxy http_proxy all_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ALL_PROXY
B="--resolve pipe.u.isucon.dev:443:127.0.0.1 -sk"
curl $B -X POST -o /dev/null -w "init %{http_code}\n" https://pipe.u.isucon.dev/api/initialize
c1=0;c3=0; sudo mysql -N -uisucon -pisucon -h 10.0.1.56 isupipe -e "select name from users where id<=50 order by id" 2>/dev/null > /tmp/names; while read n; do u=$(curl --resolve $n.u.isucon.dev:443:127.0.0.1 -sk -D - -o /dev/null https://$n.u.isucon.dev/api/tag | grep -i "^x-upstream" | tr -d "\r"); case "$u" in *10.0.1.76*) c3=$((c3+1));; *) c1=$((c1+1));; esac; done < /tmp/names; echo s1=$c1 s3=$c3
python3 - <<PY
import socket,struct,random
name="pipe.u.isucon.dev"; tid=random.randrange(65536); hdr=struct.pack(">HHHHHH",tid,0x0100,1,0,0,0)
body=b"".join(bytes([len(x)])+x.encode() for x in name.split("."))+b"\0"+struct.pack(">HH",1,1)
s=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM); s.settimeout(2); s.sendto(hdr+body,("127.0.0.1",53)); d,_=s.recvfrom(4096)
print("dns",name,"rcode",d[3]&15,"ip",socket.inet_ntoa(d[-4:]))
PY'","description":"Initialize local DNS config and verify split"}

Run13: s1 idle20% (80% used), s2 idle41% (59% used), s3 idle48% (52% used). s1 is now bottleneck-ish with local MySQL+PDNS+nginx+some app. Yet score highest 338k. s1 load average 4.39 (2 cores) due many processes/IO? But CPU idle20. Could further shift app from s1 to s3 to relieve s1, and maybe increase score. s1 app is only 20% hosts + 1/3 pipe; s1 app CPU maybe 19s over run? Top not captured during; but vmstat s1 used80%. Components: MySQL DNS maybe ~? local MySQL CPU likely high; PDNS ~? nginx ~? app ~? s1 is quite loaded. If we shift all app (pipe and hosts) to s3, s1 only nginx+PDNS+MySQL; s3 ~70%. That might relieve s1 but s3 handles more. Could improve or not.

Alternatively move DNS DB to s3? No, local on s1 seemed to improve score despite s1 high; probably because DNS latency lower and s2 freed. But s1 high load could cap at ~338. We could tune local MySQL/PDNS to reduce s1 CPU:
- DNS water torture causes many NXDOMAIN backend queries. Could enable negative cache to reduce MySQL CPU, but new user race. With local DNS and registration on s1/s3, we can implement purge? Or set `negquery-cache-ttl` small (e.g., 1s) and accept? Risk. Maybe set `negquery-cache-ttl=2`; benchmark might register then immediately resolve; if the name was queried in the previous 2s (random water torture may query it? unlikely for specific generated username) then could fail. Water torture likely uses random names, not the future username. Negative cache would help only if water torture repeats names. Stats showed 18k NXDOMAIN out of 29k queries in 114s, likely random unique; negative cache may not help. But MySQL backend queries 137k (~4.7 per query), so caching NXDOMAIN for even a fraction could help. We can inspect if water torture repeats names by analyzing `ring-nxdomain-queries` via pdns_control? PowerDNS ring buffer could show recent queries; we could inspect names to see pattern. This is allowed (server data). `pdns_control ring`? There is `pdns_control ring <name>` maybe. Could use `pdns_control show ring-nxdomain-queries`? The stats list ring-nxdomain-queries-size but not contents. `pdns_control ring` command may dump. Let's check `pdns_control help` or `pdns_control ring`. We can run after run13 to see recent NXDOMAIN names; if they repeat random, negative cache could help. But with only 2 runs left, perhaps not worth complex.

Another easy optimization: Reduce DNS query load by configuring PDNS to use `cache-ttl` for NXDOMAIN even if unique? No.

Could move PDNS/MySQL to s3 and keep s1 only nginx+app? But DNS must be on s1; could run PDNS on s3 but bind s1? no.

Could move local MySQL isudns to s3 and PDNS remote, but we already tried DNS s3 and score 326, lower. So local s1 DNS is better despite load. Maybe because DNS latency to s3 adds request latency, affecting benchmark more than CPU. Keep.

To relieve s1 CPU, shift app share further to s3 (weight higher, pipe all to s3 except initialize). s1 app currently handles ~20% hosts and 1/3 pipe; maybe app CPU ~0.2-0.3 core. Removing it might free 10-15% CPU, potentially improve if s1 saturation affects nginx/DNS. We can set hash weight s3=20 (s3 ~95%) and pipe upstream only s3 (weight 1 local? remove local from pipe; but then all pipe API except initialize go to s3). s3 handles ~95% app, s1 only nginx+DNS+MySQL. s3 app CPU currently maybe 0.5 core (52% total incl nginx); adding 20% more maybe 0.6-0.7, still headroom. s2 DB 59%, s1 frees app. This seems promising. But caution: with all pipe requests to s3, registration on s3 creates new user records pointing s3 IP; then those new users' hosts bypass s1 nginx and hit s3 nginx directly, reducing s1 nginx load too (good). s3 nginx config local, handles direct. New users ~1500 registrations, could shift substantial direct traffic from s1 nginx to s3 nginx, further relieving s1 and loading s3. s3 has headroom. This could improve significantly.
- But if s3 nginx direct traffic increases, s3 CPU maybe high; still likely okay.
- Need ensure `/api/initialize` on pipe stays local s1 (exact location).
- Pipe upstream currently has local weight1, s3 weight2. Set only s3 server (remove local) for all other pipe API. But what if s3 app down? benchmark fail, but it's up.
- Hash upstream set s3 weight maybe 20 (or remove local entirely from hash). If remove local from hash upstream, only s3 server, all wildcard hosts go s3. But existing hosts that have cached DNS all s1 nginx, so s1 nginx proxies all to s3 app; s1 still handles TLS/nginx for existing hosts. New hosts point s3 directly. s1 app would only handle initialize. That's okay. Could leave local weight1 and s3 weight20 for fallback.
- s1 local app still running; not used much. Cache clear peers: s1 initialize clears s3; s3 gets all traffic. Cross-icon invalidation to s1 unnecessary but fine.
- s1 nginx with all requests proxied to s3 adds network hop; s3 app handles. s1 nginx CPU remains high (TLS/PDNS/MySQL). But free app CPU.
- Could also reduce pipe direct by new registrations pointing s3 (already if handled s3). Good.
This single change (shift all app to s3) could help. We can test in run14. If score >338, keep for final run15. If lower, revert to run13 config for run15. We have exactly 2 runs; this is a reasonable gamble. But if run14 is worse and we revert for run15, final likely ~338. If run14 better, final even better. Let's do it.

Need modify s1 nginx config from `/tmp/isupipe-localdns.conf`:
- hash upstream: keep local weight=1, s3 weight=20 (or remove local). To ensure nearly all to s3, weight20. Test distribution sample maybe 50 -> all s3? Consistent hash with weight20 vs1 should give ~95% s3.
- pipe upstream: local weight=1, s3 weight=20, so pipe 95% s3. Or remove local. Use weight20.
- Exact initialize still local primary.
- This means s3 app handles almost all API; s1 app only initialize (and rare hash to local). s3 app cache will be fully populated; s1 app caches mostly irrelevant. s3 direct new user subdomains hit s3 nginx local; s3 nginx upstream local app. Good.
- s3 app peer URL s1; icon invalidation sends to s1 (maybe s1 caches stale but rarely serves icons for existing hosts via s1 nginx -> proxy to s3; s1 app not involved). Fine.
- s1 initialize notifies s3 clear; s3 handles all subsequent traffic with clean cache. Good.
- s3 app uses DNS DB s1 for registrations; local network. Good.
- s3 MySQL stopped, so no local DB; s3 app connects s2. Good.

Let's modify config on s1 and reload, sample distribution, then run14. No need restart apps. We should ensure s3 app can handle load; monitor. Let's do.

# /lib/systemd/system/pdns.service
[Unit]
Description=PowerDNS Authoritative Server
Documentation=man:pdns_server(1) man:pdns_control(1)
Documentation=https://doc.powerdns.com
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target mysqld.service postgresql.service slapd.service mariadb.service time-sync.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/pdns_server --guardian=no --daemon=no --disable-syslog --log-timestamp=no --write-pid=no
SyslogIdentifier=pdns_server
User=pdns
Group=pdns
Type=notify
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=1
StartLimitInterval=0
RuntimeDirectory=pdns

# Sandboxing
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE CAP_CHOWN
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE CAP_CHOWN
LockPersonality=true
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateDevices=true
PrivateTmp=true
# Setting PrivateUsers=true prevents us from opening our sockets
ProtectClock=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
ProtectHome=true
ProtectHostname=true
ProtectKernelLogs=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
# ProtectSystem=full will disallow write access to /etc and /usr, possibly
# not being able to write slaved-zones into sqlite3 or zonefiles.
ProtectSystem=full
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6
RestrictNamespaces=true
RestrictRealtime=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
SystemCallArchitectures=native
SystemCallFilter=~ @clock @debug @module @mount @raw-io @reboot @swap @cpu-emulation @obsolete
ProtectProc=invisible
PrivateIPC=true
RemoveIPC=true
DevicePolicy=closed
# Not enabled by default because it does not play well with LuaJIT
# MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# /etc/systemd/system/pdns.service.d/isudns.conf
[Unit]
After=network-online.target mysql.service mysqld.service postgresql.service slapd.service mariadb.service time-sync.target

[Service]
ProtectHome=read-only
ExecStartPost=/opt/init_zone_once.sh
